blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Home Extension Cost in Southbank in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of extending your Southbank home? Here's a realistic breakdown of costs, council fees, and timelines for Melbourne's inner south in 2026.
body: If you own a home in Southbank, you've probably looked around and thought there's room for more. A rear extension, a second storey, or even just bumping out the living room can transform how you use your space. But before you start dreaming, you need a realistic picture of what it'll cost in 2026 across Melbourne's inner suburbs.

Basic single-storey rear extensions in Southbank start around $3,000 per square metre. That's for a straightforward addition with a basic roof, standard finishes, and minimal structural changes. For a typical 40-square-metre extension, you're looking at a budget of $120,000 to $160,000. But if you're on a tricky block with easements or heritage overlays, that figure can jump.

Council approval fees in Southbank and the City of Melbourne region add another $2,000 to $8,000 depending on the complexity. You'll also need a building surveyor and an engineer, which can run $4,000 to $10,000 combined. Always factor in a 10% contingency for unexpected discoveries — dodgy stumps, asbestos, or old wiring that needs replacing.

The biggest price variable is your choice of finishes. A basic laminate kitchen versus a custom stone benchtop can make a $20,000 difference. Flooring is similar — engineered timber costs double what basic hybrid vinyl does. Our advice: splurge on structural stuff (roof, windows, insulation) and save on cosmetic things you can upgrade later.

Timelines for a typical Southbank extension are 12 to 18 weeks from start to finish. That includes demolition, slab, framing, roofing, rough-in services, internal linings, and fit-off. Delays can happen if your builder hits bad soil conditions or wet weather. A good local builder will build a few weeks of buffer into the schedule.

The best way to keep costs under control is to lock in a fixed-price contract before work starts. That way you're protected from material price hikes and scope creep. Prime Facilities offers free on-site consultations to walk through your Southbank extension and give you a no-nonsense quote. No pressure, just real numbers.

Financing your extension? Most homeowners use a mix of savings and a construction loan. Talk to your bank early — they'll want to see a fixed-price contract and a builder's insurance certificate before they release funds. We've seen clients wait weeks for approval because their paperwork wasn't ready.

Bottom line: a Southbank home extension is a solid investment if you plan carefully. Talk to a couple of builders, check their licences, and ask for recent jobs in the area. A good local builder will be happy to show you what they've done in your own street.

blogPosts.title: The Complete Guide to Commercial Fit-Outs in Melbourne CBD
blogPosts.excerpt: Planning a commercial fit-out in the CBD or Southbank? This guide covers costs, approvals, timelines, and tips from a builder who works there daily.
body: Setting up a new office, cafe, or retail space in Melbourne's CBD or Southbank is exciting, but the fit-out process can be a maze. You've got council permits, building codes, landlords, and tradies to coordinate. This guide breaks down everything you need to know for a smooth commercial fit-out in 2026.

First up, budgets. A basic commercial fit-out in Melbourne metro starts around $1,200 per square metre for a shell-suit fit-out. That covers suspended ceilings, lighting, fresh paint, carpet tiles, and a basic kitchen/break area. A mid-range fit-out with quality finishes and some joinery runs $2,000 to $2,500 per square metre.

For hospitality fit-outs like a cafe or restaurant, budgets blow out to $3,000+ per square metre because of the specialised kitchen exhaust, plumbing, and tiling. And if you're in a heritage building in the CBD, expect an extra 15% to cover conservation requirements. Always get a builder familiar with Melbourne's heritage overlays.

Approvals are a big one. You'll need a building permit from a private building surveyor, a planning permit if you're changing use, and a plumbing permit. Depending on the scope, expect 6 to 12 weeks for approvals alone. We recommend starting your permit applications before construction starts to keep your timeline tight.

Your landlord's building requirements also matter. They'll have a design and construction manual covering fire services, accessibility, and loading dock access. Failing to follow these can cost you in delays and penalties. A builder with CBD experience knows these manuals inside out and can flag issues early.

Timeline-wise, a 150-square-metre office fit-out typically takes 10 to 14 weeks from site handover to completion. That's assuming your permits are approved and materials are available. We've seen delays from imported tiles and custom joinery, so always confirm lead times before committing to a completion date.

Choosing the right builder for your Melbourne commercial fit-out makes all the difference. Look for someone who's done work in your building or a similar one, who can show you references, and who communicates clearly. Ask about their project management process — who's the point of contact and how often will you get updates?

Prime Facilities has been doing commercial fit-outs in Southbank and the CBD for over a decade. We know the ins and outs of the local council, the major landlords, and the best tradies for the job. Give us a call to discuss your fit-out — we'll talk through your budget, design, and timeline with no obligation.

blogPosts.title: Renovating a Southbank Apartment: What You Need to Know
blogPosts.excerpt: Southbank apartment renovations come with owners corporation rules and small-space challenges. Here's what to expect and how to get it right.
body: Renovating an apartment in Southbank is different from a house. You've got neighbours above, below, and beside you, plus an owners corporation with strict rules. But a well-planned renovation can transform your space and add serious value. Here's what every Southbank apartment owner needs to know before they start.

First, check your owners corporation rules. Most OC's require you to submit a renovation application with plans, a timeline, and proof of insurance. Some restrict when your tradies can work — often no noisy work before 8am or after 5pm, and no weekend work at all. Factor these rules into your schedule and budget.

Bathroom renovations are the most common Southbank apartment job, and they're tricky because of waterproofing and plumbing stack access. A full bathroom reno in a Southbank apartment costs $15,000 to $25,000 depending on the size and finish choices. You'll need a licensed waterproofing applicator and a building surveyor to sign off.

Kitchen renovations in apartments run between $12,000 and $30,000. The biggest cost is custom cabinetry to fit awkward corners and service pipes. Stick to standard appliance sizes to avoid custom joinery delays. And remember, bin and recycling storage is a requirement in most Southbank apartment OC bylaws.

Flooring is another area with OC restrictions. Many Southbank buildings require acoustic underlay to reduce noise transfer to the unit below. Engineered timber and carpet are usually okay, but laminated floating floors often get knocked back. Always check the OC's flooring policy before ordering materials.

Structural changes like knocking down a wall are rare in apartments — most internal walls are load-bearing or hide plumbing and electrical. If you do need to remove a wall, you'll need a structural engineer's report and OC approval, which can take 4 to 8 weeks. Plan around that timeline.

Storage is tight in Southbank apartments, so think about built-in joinery. Custom wardrobes, wall-to-wall shelving, and under-bench cabinets maximise every centimetre. A good carpenter can make a small apartment feel much bigger with clever storage solutions. We've seen shoe cabinets that pull out into seating.

Renovating an apartment in Southbank is absolutely worth it if you plan carefully. Work with a builder who's done apartment renovations before — they'll know the OC process, the local building surveyors, and how to keep the neighbours happy. Prime Facilities has renovated dozens of Southbank apartments and can help you navigate the process from start to finish.

blogPosts.title: 2026 Cost Guide: Bathroom Renovation in Melbourne's Inner Suburbs
blogPosts.excerpt: How much does a bathroom renovation cost in Southbank, South Yarra, and Richmond in 2026? Get the real numbers on materials, labour, and plumbing.
body: A bathroom renovation is one of the best investments you can make in your home. In Melbourne's inner suburbs like Southbank, South Yarra, and Richmond, a quality bathroom reno can recoup 80% or more of its cost at resale. But the price tag varies wildly depending on size, design, and material choices.

For a standard 4-square-metre bathroom with a shower, vanity, toilet, and bath, expect to pay between $18,000 and $28,000 in 2026. That includes demolition, waterproofing, tiling, plumbing, electrical, and new fixtures. If you're keeping the same layout (called a 'like-for-like' reno), you'll be on the lower end of that range.

Moving plumbing around adds cost fast. Relocating a toilet or shower can add $3,000 to $6,000 depending on whether you need to cut into the slab or chase walls. For apartments in Southbank, plumbing changes are especially complex because of the concrete slab construction. Always get a builder to quote the plumbing separately.

Tiling is the biggest visual cost. Basic ceramic tiles start around $40 per square metre installed, while large-format porcelain can run $120 to $200 per square metre. Feature tiles — like a herringbone splashback or a mosaic floor — push that higher. A good tiler will spend 10+ days on a standard bathroom, so the labour is significant.

Fixtures and fittings are where people blow their budget. A basic mixer tap set costs $200, but a high-end German brand can cost $1,500. Same for toilets: $400 for a basic model, $2,000+ for a wall-hung rimless unit. We advise clients to spend on the showerhead and taps (you use them every day) and save on the towel rail and toilet roll holder.

Waterproofing is non-negotiable and must be done by a licensed waterproofing applicator. It costs around $1,500 to $3,000 for a standard bathroom and includes a 7-year guarantee. Don't let anyone skip it — a failed waterproofing job will cost you $10,000+ in repairs to the unit below in an apartment building.

Timeline for a bathroom renovation in Melbourne's inner suburbs is 4 to 6 weeks. That's a week for demolition, 2 weeks for waterproofing and tiling (with drying time), 1 week for plumbing and electrical rough-in, and 1 week for fit-off. Add another week if you're doing custom joinery like a vanity cabinet.

Choosing the right builder for your bathroom renovation is crucial. Look for someone who's done apartments, knows the local council requirements, and has a portfolio of recent work. Prime Facilities offers a fixed-price quote for your Southbank bathroom renovation, including all materials and labour, with no surprises. Give us a call for a chat.
